speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when you first noticed the swelling and pain in your right ring finger, and has anything specific triggered it?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the finger appear crooked or rotated compared to the others, and is there any visible bruising or an open wound? Can you still bend the finger at all, or does it feel completely stuck?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex the distal joint after that specific injury strongly suggests a rupture of the flexor tendon, often called a jersey finger. Does the tip of your finger feel numb, or is the sensation intact? Can you make a fist and keep the finger curled, or does it immediately spring back straight?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any numbness or tingling in the tip of your right ring finger, and does the finger spring back to a straight position immediately when you try to curl it? Based on your history of the finger getting caught in a jersey and the inability to flex the distal joint, I suspect a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion. I will now request a test to confirm this. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray rules out a fracture, which aligns with my suspicion of a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion, commonly known as a jersey finger. Since the tendon has likely detached and retracted, surgery is often required to prevent permanent loss of function. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Tendon Avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
